questions.question: You have a batched input tensor X with shape [B, T, d_model] and a weight matrix W with shape [d_model, d_out]. What is the shape of the output Y when computing Y = X @ W using a batched GEMM?
questions.choice_A: [B, T, d_out]
questions.choice_B: [B, d_model, d_out]
questions.choice_C: [T, d_out]
questions.choice_D: [B, T, d_model, d_out]

questions.question: Why do deep learning frameworks avoid forming explicit Jacobian matrices for layers like Y = X @ W during backpropagation?
questions.choice_A: Because Jacobians are theoretically undefined for matrix operations
questions.choice_B: Forming Jacobians is memory- and compute-inefficient; vector-Jacobian products can compute gradients without materializing the full Jacobian
questions.choice_C: Because the chain rule only applies to scalar functions
questions.choice_D: Because GEMM kernels cannot be differentiated

questions.question: In backpropagation through a linear layer Y = X @ W, given upstream gradient dY, which expression correctly gives the gradient with respect to W?
questions.choice_A: dW = dY @ X
questions.choice_B: dW = X @ dY
questions.choice_C: dW = X^T @ dY
questions.choice_D: dW = dY^T @ X

questions.question: Consider multi-head attention with queries Q, keys K, and values V shaped [B, H, T, d_h]. The attention weights A are softmax(Q K^T / sqrt(d_h)). Which statement about gradient flow is most accurate?
questions.choice_A: Gradients flow only through V because A is non-differentiable
questions.choice_B: Gradients flow through V but not Q or K due to the temperature scaling
questions.choice_C: Gradients flow through Q and K but not V because values are not used in the softmax
questions.choice_D: Gradients flow through Q, K, V, and the softmax; the softmax’s Jacobian couples positions within each attention distribution

questions.question: Which broadcasting rule is typically applied when adding a bias vector b of shape [d_out] to a batched output Y of shape [B, T, d_out]?
questions.choice_A: b is broadcast across the first two dimensions, adding the same vector to each [d_out] slice
questions.choice_B: b must be reshaped to [B, d_out, T] before addition
questions.choice_C: b is appended as a new dimension, yielding [B, T, d_out, 1]
questions.choice_D: Broadcasting is not supported for bias addition in batched outputs

questions.question: In a computation graph, why are certain intermediate activations saved during the forward pass?
questions.choice_A: To reduce model size during inference
questions.choice_B: They are needed to compute local gradients during the backward pass efficiently
questions.choice_C: They are used to reorder operations for numerical stability only
questions.choice_D: They are required only if the model uses nonlinearity

questions.question: For the linear transformation Y = X @ W + b, with X: [B, T, d_in], W: [d_in, d_out], b: [d_out], and upstream gradient dY: [B, T, d_out], what is the shape of dX?
questions.choice_A: [d_in, d_out]
questions.choice_B: [B, T, d_out]
questions.choice_C: [B, T, d_in]
questions.choice_D: [B, d_in]

questions.question: What is the main advantage of using vector-Jacobian products (VJP) in reverse-mode automatic differentiation?
questions.choice_A: They avoid the need for the chain rule in composite functions
questions.choice_B: They allow computing gradients of many outputs with respect to one input efficiently
questions.choice_C: They compute gradients of one scalar output with respect to many inputs efficiently
questions.choice_D: They preclude the need for saving any activations

questions.question: In batched matrix multiplication for attention, you often compute scores S = Q @ K^T with Q and K shaped [B, H, T, d_h]. What is the shape of S?
questions.choice_A: [B, H, T, T]
questions.choice_B: [B, T, d_h, T]
questions.choice_C: [B, H, d_h, d_h]
questions.choice_D: [B, T, T, H]

questions.question: Which statement best describes gradient shapes through the projection matrices in attention (W_Q, W_K, W_V) when the input X has shape [B, T, d_model] and W_Q has shape [d_model, H d_h]?
questions.choice_A: dW_Q has shape [B, T, d_model, H d_h]
questions.choice_B: dW_Q has shape [d_model, H d_h], aggregated over batch and time via a sum
questions.choice_C: dW_Q has shape [H, d_model, d_h]
questions.choice_D: dW_Q has shape [d_model, d_model]

questions.question: When implementing backpropagation through a GEMM on GPUs, which operation typically appears due to the chain rule?
questions.choice_A: Elementwise inversion of the input matrix
questions.choice_B: Transposed GEMM (e.g., using W^T or X^T) to align dimensions for gradient accumulation
questions.choice_C: Matrix determinant calculation
questions.choice_D: Solving a linear system for each batch element

questions.question: Consider the memory-time tradeoff known as activation checkpointing. What does it do?
questions.choice_A: Stores all activations and recomputes nothing during backward, maximizing speed
questions.choice_B: Deletes model weights and reloads them per layer to save memory
questions.choice_C: Recomputes selected forward activations during backward to reduce peak memory usage
questions.choice_D: Quantizes gradients to 8-bit during forward to reduce memory

questions.question: In vectorized computation, what is the primary benefit of arranging operations as large batched tensor kernels (e.g., one GEMM) rather than many small loops?
questions.choice_A: It improves gradient accuracy but reduces numerical stability
questions.choice_B: It increases parallelism and hardware utilization, reducing overheads
questions.choice_C: It eliminates the need for autodiff frameworks
questions.choice_D: It prevents overfitting by randomizing computation

questions.question: In reverse-mode autodiff, why is it efficient for training neural networks with a scalar loss?
questions.choice_A: It computes gradients of many inputs with respect to one scalar output in a single backward pass
questions.choice_B: It computes gradients of one input with respect to many outputs simultaneously
questions.choice_C: It avoids storing any intermediate activations
questions.choice_D: It only requires computing the Jacobian once and reusing it

questions.question: For Y = X @ W with X: [B, T, d_in], W: [d_in, d_out], which expression correctly gives the gradient with respect to X given dY?
questions.choice_A: dX = dY @ W
questions.choice_B: dX = W @ dY
questions.choice_C: dX = dY @ W^T
questions.choice_D: dX = W^T @ dY^T

questions.question: Which statement about broadcasting semantics is correct when multiplying a tensor A: [B, 1, d] with a tensor B: [1, T, d] elementwise?
questions.choice_A: Broadcasting is impossible because two dimensions are 1
questions.choice_B: The result has shape [B, T, 1]
questions.choice_C: The result has shape [B, T, d], with singleton dimensions broadcast along B and T
questions.choice_D: One must explicitly tile both tensors to the same shape before multiplication

questions.question: In attention, the softmax is applied along the last T dimension of scores S: [B, H, T, T]. What is a key property of the softmax Jacobian relevant for backpropagation?
questions.choice_A: It is diagonal, so gradients do not couple different positions
questions.choice_B: It is symmetric positive definite with constant entries
questions.choice_C: It couples positions within the same row: dsoftmax/dz has terms p_i (delta_{ij} - p_j)
questions.choice_D: It is unitary, preserving vector norms during backpropagation

questions.question: Which best characterizes a Jacobian-vector product (JVP) compared to a vector-Jacobian product (VJP)?
questions.choice_A: JVP propagates tangent perturbations forward; VJP propagates sensitivities backward
questions.choice_B: JVP is used only for scalar-valued functions; VJP is used only for vector-valued functions
questions.choice_C: JVP requires storing all activations; VJP does not
questions.choice_D: JVP is numerically unstable, unlike VJP

questions.question: In an LLM block, you compute Q = X @ W_Q, K = X @ W_K, V = X @ W_V. If an upstream gradient arrives at the attention output and backpropagates to Q, which path must be considered when computing gradients with respect to W_Q?
questions.choice_A: Only the direct path from Q to the attention output; gradients through K and V are irrelevant for W_Q
questions.choice_B: The path through the softmax(Q K^T) since Q interacts with K in the score computation
questions.choice_C: Only the path through V because Q and V are multiplied
questions.choice_D: No path exists; Q is detached before attention

questions.question: During the backward pass of Y = X @ W + b with bias b: [d_out], how is db computed from dY: [B, T, d_out]?
questions.choice_A: db = sum over B and T of dY, yielding [d_out]
questions.choice_B: db = mean over B and T of dY, yielding [d_out]
questions.choice_C: db = dY @ 1, yielding [B, T, d_out]
questions.choice_D: db cannot be computed due to broadcasting

questions.question: Which statement about associativity in matrix chains is most relevant for efficient GEMM-based forward and backward passes?
questions.choice_A: Matrix multiplication is commutative, so we can reorder terms arbitrarily
questions.choice_B: Associativity allows choosing parenthesization to minimize flop count and memory traffic
questions.choice_C: Associativity is irrelevant when batching is present
questions.choice_D: Changing parenthesization changes the mathematical result
